front.title: Agent Execution Evidence: A SCITT Profile for Verifiable Records of AI Agent Runs
front.workgroup: Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust

abstract.t: AI agents act through calls to models, tools and other agents. Identity work establishes who an agent is and what it may do, but leaves execution-evidence formats and assurance criteria out of scope. This document profiles the Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency, and Trust (SCITT) architecture for Signed Statements that bind an agent's registered identity, declared capabilities, risk-based assessment and supervised operational status to a hash-chained record of every call the agent makes. It also defines admission records produced where a call is received, and the linking of records for requests that pass between agents of different operators. It specifies Registration Policy, offline verification and Bundle requirements. It does not define an accreditation scheme, a universal risk classification, an identifier scheme or a policy language.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: An AI agent is a workload whose behaviour is driven, in whole or in part, by a non-deterministic decision process, typically a large language model (LLM), and which acts on the world by invoking tools, services and resources. Every consequential thing an agent does passes through one of two doors: a call to a model (an inference) or a call to a tool. If evidence is produced at those two doors, bound to the agent's identity and to the policy in force, and registered in an append-only, non-equivocating log, a third party can later establish what the agent did, under which rules, and with which configuration, without trusting the operator's own logs.

The WIMSE AI Identity Management System describes how agent identities are established, credentials provisioned and authorization decisions made. It requires tamper-evident audit logs with a minimum set of fields (Section 11) but leaves the format of those logs open; it states that posture evidence formats (Section 8), the policy model and document format (Section 12) and compliance criteria (Section 13) are out of scope. The audit architecture in identifies SCITT Signed Statements, Receipts and Transparent Statements as the canonical artifacts for non-repudiable custody of audit records and lists a SCITT registration policy profile as a work item. This document is a concrete proposal for that profile. It builds on the WIMSE architecture : agents are workloads in its sense, and their runtime identities are WIMSE workload identifiers .
Several individual drafts already profile SCITT for agent actions (). Each records that an action happened and its disposition. Four gaps remain that this profile addresses:

list.t: An identity that a party other than the operator vouches for, bound to a per-call evidence chain. A workload identifier proves which software is making a call, but the operator of that software issues it to itself, within its own trust domain. It does not say which agent the software is, who is accountable for it, or whether it is the agent that was assessed, and an agent that runs in several environments has several unrelated identifiers (Section 3.1.2 of ). This profile separates a long-term agent identity, issued by an Agent Registration Authority that Relying Parties accept, from the runtime identities under which the operator's software authenticates (). An Agent Credential Statement records which runtime identities belong to the agent, and every Execution Receipt carries the runtime identifier, the preceding record hash and optionally a per-call agent signature, so that a chain of receipts is bound to one registered agent and cannot be spliced.

Integrity of instruction files, system prompts and tool manifests. An agent's behaviour is determined as much by its system prompt, instruction files, skills, hooks, tool manifests and memory as by its model, and injection through these inputs, including through invisible Unicode, is a documented attack class. This profile defines a Configuration Integrity Statement that commits to digests of the static inputs after mandatory Unicode normalization, requires every Execution Receipt to reference the configuration in force, and commits to the state of memory at the start and end of each Task.

Revocable operational assurance bound to running evidence, under supervision. An assessment is useful only while the assessed identity, capabilities, policy, configuration and deployment remain applicable. This profile binds an Assurance Statement to those values, records its risk basis and monitoring coverage, and lets a Supervisory Authority, separate from the assessor, restrict, suspend or withdraw it.

Evidence where a call is received, and across calls between agents. Agents increasingly call services operated by other parties, and those services are increasingly agents themselves. A request can pass through several agents, each run by a different operator, before it reaches the system that acts on it. For example, an assistant acting for an individual asks a platform's agent to file an application; that agent queries a records service; the records service calls an identity-verification service. Records produced only on the calling side cannot support the decision made on the serving side, and records kept separately on each side cannot show that they describe the same call.

section.t: A Serving Party decides on every call whether to act. It is the only party that can apply its own conditions whatever the caller's operator does, but it sees one call at a time and not the history that led to it. The decision is made per call, not per session or per credential, because what it depends on changes between calls: an agent's assurance can be suspended within minutes, one agent can act for many Principals with different permissions, and operations on the same service carry different risk. This profile therefore defines an admission record that a Serving Party produces for every call it receives, stating what it checked and what it decided. That record is the Serving Party's evidence of its own conduct and gives an auditor a second, independent record of the call. Only the caller's record shows why a call was made; only the Serving Party's record shows what was admitted and on what basis; comparing the two, when both parties' chains are verified together, shows a call that either side omitted.

When a request passes through intermediaries, four questions need answers that no single hop's record supplies: which agent originated the request and for which Principal; whether any intermediary used authority broader than that Principal's; whether suspending an agent stops the work it started further along; and which operator's agent did what. The WIMSE architecture requires that "each hop in the chain MUST explicitly scope and re-bind the security context" and that autonomous actions "MUST be clearly distinguished from delegated ones" (Section 3.4.11 of ). This profile links each hop's records to those of the hop before it and carries the principal of the transaction, a transaction identifier and the sequence of acting agents with the request, so that a verifier can answer these questions from evidence rather than from the operators' accounts. The receipts show what each hop recorded and on what basis it was admitted; showing that no intermediary used authority broader than the Principal's needs, in addition, a common representation of scopes ().

A declared objective, attested runtime and guardrails do not constrain every means an agent may choose. During a 2026 cyber-capability evaluation, agents created an unsanctioned coordination channel, pursued scorer tampering, crossed task boundaries and investigated altering their traces . This motivates third-party review of whether capabilities and controls are proportionate to purpose.

Monitoring is a distinct safeguard after assessment: for highly autonomous or otherwise higher-risk agents, it checks observed operation against the assessed scope and approved controls and supports reassessment, suspension or withdrawal. Article 72 of requires proportionate lifetime monitoring for legally classified high-risk AI systems. This profile's higher_risk value is not that legal classification and does not establish compliance.

This document is a profile of and . It does not change the SCITT architecture and does not define an identifier scheme, how a registry or Supervisory Authority is established, a policy language or an accreditation scheme.

section.name: Requirements Notation
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: This document uses the terms Artifact, Issuer, Receipt, Registration, Registration Policy, Relying Party, Signed Statement, Statement, Transparency Service (TS), Transparent Statement and Verifiable Data Structure (VDS) as defined in ; Workload, Trust Domain and Workload Identity Credential as described in ; Actor and Delegation as in Sections 1.1 and 4.1 of ; and Call Chain and Transaction as defined in , except that a Call Chain here may cross Trust Domains. The principal of the transaction is the subject named by the sub claim of a Transaction Token (). This profile uses delegation semantics only, never impersonation.

The terms below are either profiled from existing IETF vocabulary, as stated in each definition, or introduced by this document. Agent Registration Authority, Calling Agent, Caller Reference, Linked Evidence Chains, Linked Verification, Principal Link, Responsible Entity, Serving Party, Sub-agent and Supervisory Authority have no equivalent in the IETF specifications cited here.

dd.t: The ordered list of Actors that have acted on a request, least recent first. It is the list form of a chain of delegation expressed by nested act claims (): the most deeply nested act is the first entry and the outermost act, the current actor, is the last. The term "actor chain" is used in . It records attribution, not authority ().
The authorization decision a Serving Party makes for one call, recorded as an Execution Receipt of type admission (). It is a policy decision in the sense of , made per call and recorded.
A workload whose behaviour is driven, in whole or in part, by a non-deterministic decision process (typically an LLM) and that invokes tools, services or resources, as in Section 4 of .

A SCITT Issuer that evaluates an agent and issues Assurance Statements (). It MAY be the Responsible Entity at assurance levels 1 and 2. At levels 3 and 4 it MUST be a Third-Party Agent Assurance Assessor.

A SCITT Issuer that issues long-term agent identities: it verifies the Responsible Entity, records what was declared for the agent, assigns the logical_agent_id and lineage_id, and maintains the registration's status (). How an authority is established is out of scope. The name is unrelated to SCITT Registration, which is the act of entering a Signed Statement into a TS.
A self-contained set of Transparent Statements and Execution Receipts sufficient for offline verification of a segment of an Evidence Chain ().
The member of an admission receipt that identifies the Calling Agent's Execution Receipt for the same call ().

For a given call, the agent that makes it, and the workload, possibly itself an agent, that receives it and decides whether to act on it. These are roles in one call, not kinds of agent: an agent is a Serving Party for the call it receives and a Calling Agent for the calls it then makes. In the terms of , the Calling Agent is the current actor. A Serving Party that verifies evidence before admitting a call acts as a Relying Party.

The operator's declaration of an agent's purpose and effective model, tool, data, permission and delegation scope, including the functions of any Sub-agents, committed to by digest at registration and in an Assurance Statement.

A point at which a call is intercepted, a policy decision taken and enforced, and an Execution Receipt produced. It combines a Policy Decision Point and a Policy Enforcement Point () and adds recording. In a Harness these are the model door (every inference) and the tool door (every tool invocation, its result and any resulting egress); at a Serving Party, the ingress door (every call received).
An ordered sequence of Execution Receipts, each carrying the hash of its predecessor, scoped to one Agent Credential or Serving Party Credential Statement ().

The service, operated by or for the Harness or Serving Party operator, that issues Execution Receipt and Execution Epoch Statements and registers them with a TS; the SCITT Issuer for those statements.
A single record produced at a Decision Point (); registered with a TS, individually or through an epoch root, it becomes an Execution Receipt Statement.
The runtime that hosts an agent, mediates its calls to models and tools, and operates the Decision Points.
The Evidence Chains of the parties to one Call Chain, linked through Caller References; and their verification together ().

The persistent identity of an agent across environments, named by a logical_agent_id issued by an Agent Registration Authority; and a workload identifier () under which the agent authenticates in one Trust Domain for one period. A Logical Agent is a logical workload in the sense of that is an agent. One Logical Agent MAY have several Runtime Identities.
Time-bounded confidence that an identified agent's assessed capabilities, deployment and controls remain within their approved scope, based on assessment and, where required, continuing monitoring.
A versioned document that configures Decision Points, layered by digest reference to a parent (). The policy document format is out of scope.
The natural person, organization or workload on whose behalf an agent acts for a given Task. It is the "delegated subject (user or system)" of Section 11 of , and is used as in .
A digest that lets the two parties to a call show that they recorded the same Principal without revealing it ().
The legal or natural person accountable for a Logical Agent, as registered in its Agent Registration Statement.
An agent instantiated by another agent, its parent, to perform a declared function within the parent's Tasks. A Sub-agent has no Logical Agent identity of its own and acts under its parent's ().

The Issuer that a Relying Party's or TS's policy designates for a scheme named by scheme_id. It publishes the scheme, holds the status of Assurance Statements issued under it, and alone restricts, suspends or withdraws them ().
A unit of agent work delimited by task_start and task_end Execution Receipts and named by the seq of its task_start.

An Agent Assurance Assessor that is organizationally independent of the Responsible Entity and agent operator, and whose identity and signing key a Relying Party accepts under its trust policy. This profile-specific role can perform the RATS Verifier role or consume Attestation Results from an accepted RATS Verifier, but also assesses the agent's capabilities, deployment and controls. Existing IETF specifications do not define qualification, independence-testing or accreditation criteria for this role.

section.t: This profile defines eleven Signed Statement types: Agent Registration, Model Provider, Agent Credential, Serving Party Credential, Policy Pack, Configuration Integrity, Configuration Drift, Execution Receipt, Execution Epoch, Assurance and Revocation Statements ( to ).

section.name: Identifiers
section.t: This profile imports identifier schemes and does not define one.

dd.t: MUST be a did:web identifier whose domain name, the first component of the method-specific identifier after percent-decoding, equals the host component of the iss of the Agent Registration Statement that assigned it, for example did:web:register.example:agent:a1b2c3 issued by https://register.example. The identifier itself thus shows which authority vouches for the agent.

SHOULD be a Workload Identifier as defined in (the spiffe or wimse scheme). Section 6 of requires that an agent be assigned exactly one WIMSE identifier; within any one such deployment, that identifier is the agent's Runtime Identity there, and the Logical Agent sits above the Runtime Identities of all its deployments.
A URI under a domain that the Serving Party controls, using the https, spiffe, wimse or did:web scheme.

section.t: Implementations MUST treat all identifiers as opaque strings for comparison purposes; two identifiers are equal if and only if their octet sequences are equal.

The CWT Claims header parameter (label 15) required by MUST carry the Issuer in iss (label 1). In sub (label 2), Agent Credential, Configuration Integrity, Configuration Drift, Execution Receipt and Execution Epoch Statements carry the applicable Runtime Identity (or service_id); Agent Registration and Assurance Statements carry logical_agent_id; Serving Party Credential Statements carry service_id; Model Provider Statements carry model_id; Policy Pack Statements carry pack_id; and Revocation Statements repeat the sub of the statement revoked.

A Principal is carried as a claim inside the statement payload, not in the COSE header, because a Principal is not an Artifact subject in the SCITT sense and because the header is visible to the TS. A Principal of kind natural person MUST be represented by a 32-octet digest computed as SHA-256 over the concatenation of a pepper held by the statement's Issuer and the canonical identifier of the person (). A Principal of kind organization or workload MAY be represented in clear text.

section.name: Agent Identification
section.t: A Relying Party that must decide whether to act on an agent's request, or hold someone accountable afterwards, needs an identity that persists across environments and that a party other than the operator vouches for. This profile obtains it in the following steps.

list.t: Declaration. The operator submits to an Agent Registration Authority the agent's Capability Profile and, for each model in it, the Model Provider Statement () where the provider has issued one. The Capability Profile identifies each model by a dated version identifier and, where available, by the digest of that statement.

Verification. The authority verifies the Responsible Entity by its own identity-proofing procedures, which are out of scope. It SHOULD require the operator to prove possession, at registration, of the agent key it will name in its first Agent Credential Statement.

Registration. The authority issues an Agent Registration Statement () assigning the logical_agent_id and lineage_id and committing to what was declared, and registers it on a TS. The registered statement is the authoritative record of the agent's identity.

Operation. The operator issues Agent Credential Statements () that reference the registration and list the agent's Runtime Identities, key, Harness, model binding and Sub-agents. These change as the agent moves between environments and its keys rotate; the registration does not.

Status. The authority maintains the registration's status in a Token Status List and ends it, where required, with a Revocation Statement: reason code 5 (closed) for administrative retirement and 3 (withdrawn) for an adverse finding.

Change and lineage. A change to the declared Capability Profile, or a new Model Provider Statement for a model in it, requires a superseding Agent Registration Statement with the same logical_agent_id and lineage_id, and reassessment; the authority MUST revoke the superseded registration with reason code 2 (superseded), so that credentials naming it cease to verify. A change of Responsible Entity, for example on a transfer between organizations, requires a new registration with a new logical_agent_id and the same lineage_id; the previous registration is closed, and the agent MUST be reassessed before use. The lineage_id keeps the history of earlier registrations, adverse entries included, linked to the agent.

section.t: A Relying Party is configured with the set of Agent Registration Authorities it accepts. An agent registered by an authority in another jurisdiction is verified identically and accepted only if that authority is in the set; how authorities come to recognize one another is out of scope. An organization MAY act as the Agent Registration Authority for its own agents; whether a Relying Party accepts it is a matter of policy.
An Agent Registration Authority MAY also publish registrations through other channels. Such channels are not authoritative: the registered statement and its status prevail.

section.name: Common Encoding
section.t: Each statement type defined here is a CBOR map with integer keys. Hash algorithm identifiers are taken from the IANA COSE Algorithms registry. The CDDL in this document uses the conventions of . Every payload is encoded with the deterministic encoding rules of ("canonical CBOR" below).

In the JSON form, kind determines whether id is a base64url digest or a clear-text identifier. principal_assurance records how strongly the Principal's identity was verified, using the identity proofing dimension of ; each jurisdiction's trust framework, named by the trustmark, defines the values, so that Principals proofed under different trust frameworks are recorded by the same mechanism. delegation_ref lets one Principal's delegation be revoked without revoking the agent: its status entry is maintained by whoever granted the delegation. Both are fixed for a Task, as the rest of principal is ().

No statement defined here contains a floating-point value, and an Issuer MUST NOT emit one, including NaN or an infinity. Text strings MUST be valid UTF-8. A payload that violates either rule, or that has duplicate map keys, is malformed: an Issuer MUST NOT repair it before signing or hashing, and a TS or Relying Party MUST reject it.

Each statement is carried as the payload of a COSE_Sign1 Signed Statement per . The protected header MUST contain alg (label 1); content type (label 3) set to application/aee-statement+cbor or application/aee-statement+json; kid (label 4), x5t (label 34) or x5chain (label 33) per ; and the CWT Claims header parameter (label 15) with iss, sub and the aee_type claim (), whose value MUST equal key 1 of the payload. Duplicating the type in the header lets a TS apply type-specific Registration Policy () from the non-opaque header, as requires, without parsing the payload.

section.name: JSON Alternative Encoding
section.t: A statement MAY instead be encoded as a JSON object. Each integer key is replaced by the member name given for it in the CDDL comment of its type (for example key 7 of an Execution Receipt is policy_pack_digest); group names such as principal, harness, model_binding, validity, runtime_identities and assessed_scope name nested objects, and enumerated values use the lowercase names of their CDDL group. Byte strings are base64url without padding, and a digest is an object {"alg": <name>, "value": <base64url>} where <name> is a hash name from the IANA "Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry" (for example "sha-256"). The JSON form MUST be I-JSON , which excludes lone surrogates and duplicate member names, and integers in it MUST NOT exceed 2^53 - 1 in absolute value. Before signing or hashing, it MUST be canonicalized with . The content type is application/aee-statement+json. A single Evidence Chain MUST use one encoding throughout.

section.name: Agent Registration Statement
section.t: An Agent Registration Statement is the authoritative record of a Logical Agent's identity (). Its Issuer is an Agent Registration Authority.

figure.sourcecode: agent-registration = { 1 => 9, ; aee-type 2 => tstr, ; logical_agent_id (see {{ids}}) 3 => principal, ; responsible_entity 4 => tstr, ; lineage_id 5 => digest, ; capability_profile_digest, as declared 6 => [ * digest ], ; provider_statement_digests 7 => validity, ; validity ? 8 => status-ref, ; status: Token Status List reference ? 9 => tstr, ; scheme_id: registration scheme (URI) ? 10 => digest ; prior_registration_digest }

section.t: capability_profile_digest commits to the Capability Profile the operator declared, and provider_statement_digests to the payloads of the Model Provider Statements it references. lineage_id is an opaque identifier assigned by the authority that outlives logical_agent_id. prior_registration_digest names the registration this one supersedes or, on a change of Responsible Entity, follows. A natural-person responsible_entity is hashed with a pepper held by the authority ().

section.name: Model Provider Statement
section.t: A Model Provider Statement records what a model provider states about one version of a model. Its Issuer is the model provider. An operator SHOULD reference one for every model in its Capability Profile where the provider has issued one; a Supervisory Authority's scheme or a Relying Party MAY require it.

figure.sourcecode: model-provider = { 1 => 11, ; aee-type 2 => tstr, ; model_id: dated version identifier 3 => tstr, ; provider ? 4 => digest, ; weights_digest 5 => digest, ; evaluations_digest 6 => digest, ; safeguards_digest 7 => [ + tstr ], ; permitted_uses ? 8 => digest, ; training_data_summary_digest ? 9 => digest, ; change_commitments_digest 10 => uint ; iat, seconds since the Unix epoch }

section.t: model_id MUST be a dated version identifier, never an alias that the provider can repoint. evaluations_digest commits to the provider's capability and dangerous-capability evaluations, and safeguards_digest to the safeguards applied. The documents are retained by the provider; their formats are out of scope. A new model version or weights digest requires a new statement and, for any agent using it, a superseding registration and reassessment ().

section.name: Agent Credential Statement
section.t: An Agent Credential Statement binds an agent identifier to the public key the agent uses for per-call signatures, to the Principal it acts for, to the Harness that hosts it, and to how its model is bound. It also records the agent's identity continuity: which registered Logical Agent this runtime is an instance of, and under which Runtime Identities it and its Sub-agents may appear. Its Issuer is the Harness operator or the identity provider that issued the agent's workload credential.

The continuity fields exist because workload identifiers do not, by themselves, say what they name. Section 3.1.2 of states that a workload identifier "MAY represent a logical workload, a service implemented by one or more workloads, or a specific workload instance, depending on deployment policy", and that "two credentials containing the same workload identifier value represent the same workload only when validated under the same trust domain and issuer trust configuration". An agent that moves between a development cluster, a production cluster and a cloud identity platform acquires a different identifier in each, meaningful only within its trust domain. A Relying Party cannot correlate those identifiers by inspection. This profile therefore records the mapping from a Logical Agent to its Runtime Identities as a signed, registered statement, and verifies receipts against it, rather than assuming correlation.

The binding modes have the following meaning. weights-digest: the Harness loads the model locally and weights_digest commits to the weights. api: the model is invoked through a remote API; only model_id and provider are known. api-tee: as api, but the provider supplies attestation Evidence for the serving environment, referenced by tee_evidence. Relying Parties MUST NOT infer from mode api anything about which model actually served a request; only the provider's claim is recorded.

registration_digest names the Agent Registration Statement in force. logical_agent_id and responsible_entity MUST equal those of that registration. provider_statement_digest, where present, names the Model Provider Statement for the bound model and MUST be among the registration's provider_statement_digests. runtime_identities lists every identifier under which the agent may produce Execution Receipts while this credential is valid, each with its scheme, trust domain and validity window. The agent_id in key 2 MUST appear in runtime_identities. lifecycle_class is ephemeral for an agent instantiated for one Task and persistent for a long-running agent. subagents lists the Sub-agents the agent may instantiate (). hosts is used only where the agent is a Serving Party. It has the meaning and the form defined for the Serving Party Credential Statement in , and the same rule applies: it MUST be present in an Agent Credential Statement whose Evidence Chain contains an admission receipt that carries call_digest. An agent that only calls other parties needs no hosts.

An Agent Credential Statement is valid for Execution Receipts whose ts lies within its validity. Rotation of the agent key is performed by registering a new Agent Credential Statement; the old statement remains valid for receipts within its own window.

section.name: Sub-agents
section.t: A Sub-agent acts under its parent's identity and credential; it is not separately registered. Each function a Sub-agent may perform MUST be declared in the parent's Capability Profile, so that the assessment covers it, and each Sub-agent MUST be listed in the parent's Agent Credential Statement with a subagent_ref unique within the parent and its declared function. A Sub-agent that runs as a separate workload SHOULD have its own subagent_key and Runtime Identities, so that compromise of one Sub-agent does not expose the parent's key. Every Execution Receipt produced for a Sub-agent carries subagent (), so that each action is attributable to a specific Sub-agent and function. A Sub-agent's work is a Task delegated from a Task of its parent (). An agent that outlives its parent, or that serves other agents, is not a Sub-agent and MUST be registered in its own right.

section.name: Serving Party Credential Statement
section.t: A Serving Party that is itself an agent uses its Agent Credential Statement. A Serving Party that is not an agent scopes its Evidence Chain with a Serving Party Credential Statement, whose Issuer is the Serving Party's operator.

figure.sourcecode: serving-party-credential = { 1 => 10, ; aee-type 2 => tstr, ; service_id (see {{ids}}) 3 => COSE_Key, ; service_key 4 => principal, ; responsible_entity 5 => validity, ; validity ? 6 => [ + runtime-identity ], ; runtime_identities ? 7 => [ + tstr ] ; hosts }

section.t: The agent_id of each receipt in the chain carries the service_id or one of the listed runtime_identities. A Serving Party Credential is not registered by an Agent Registration Authority; the Serving Party identifies itself under its own domain.

hosts lists every host under which callers may reach the service, including the names of fronting gateways and proxies. Each entry is in the form of egress_host (): a lowercase A-label with no port. A caller's egress_host is compared with this list in Linked Verification (). The comparison shows that the caller named a host this Serving Party declares. It does not show which service the caller meant when one host fronts several services, because each of them lists that host. Behind a shared host, services are told apart by the request-target, which call_digest binds, and by the gateway's routing, which this document does not record. hosts MUST be present in a Serving Party Credential Statement whose Evidence Chain contains an admission receipt that carries call_digest; there is no default, and the host of service_id is not assumed. Each entry MUST be a host that the operator controls or has delegated to its front end. The list is the Serving Party's own signed declaration; says what follows from a false one.

section.name: Policy Pack Statement
section.t: A Policy Pack Statement commits to the digest of a policy document and places it in a lineage. Its Issuer is the pack author. The format of the policy document is out of scope; the digest is over the document bytes as published.

figure.sourcecode: policy-pack = { 1 => 2, ; aee-type 2 => tstr, ; pack_id (URI or opaque name) 3 => tstr, ; pack_version 4 => digest, ; pack_digest over the pack document ? 5 => digest, ; parent_pack_digest 6 => layer, ; layer ? 7 => tstr ; pack_content_type of the document } layer = &( jurisdiction: 1, sector: 2, institution: 3, deployment: 4 )

section.t: Policy Packs form a chain from the most general to the most specific layer (jurisdiction, sector, institution, deployment). A pack with a parent_pack_digest MUST have a layer strictly greater than its parent's. A child pack can only tighten: for every Decision Point and every input, the decision under the child MUST NOT be less restrictive than under any ancestor, with restrictiveness ordered block > confirm > record > allow (). A Relying Party MUST walk the parent chain to a root and verify that every pack is registered (); whether a child semantically tightens its parent cannot be established offline from digests, and an Assurance Statement () is how a party asserts it.

section.name: Configuration Integrity Statement
section.t: A Configuration Integrity Statement commits to the digests of the inputs that shape an agent's behaviour other than the model and the policy. Its Issuer is the Evidence Service.

figure.sourcecode:
config-integrity = { 1 => 3, ; aee-type 2 => tstr, ; agent_id 3 => [ + config-entry ], ; entries, ordered by name (octet order) 4 => digest, ; config_digest over canonical entries 5 => uint, ; normalization, 1 or 2 (below) 6 => uint ; iat, seconds since the Unix epoch } config-entry = [ name: tstr, ; path or logical name value: digest, ; digest of the normalized content class: config-class ] config-class = &( system_prompt: 1, instruction_file: 2, skill: 3, hook: 4, mcp_config: 5, tool_manifest: 6, tool_description: 7 )
config-drift = { 1 => 4, ; aee-type 2 => tstr, ; agent_id 3 => digest, ; prev_config_digest 4 => digest, ; new_config_digest 5 => [ + drift-entry ], ; changes 6 => uint ; iat } drift-entry = [ name: tstr, class: config-class, change: &( added: 1, modified: 2, removed: 3 ), ? old: digest, ? new: digest ]

section.t: Memory written by the agent at runtime is not configuration: it changes between and within Tasks, and committing it here would require new statements before every call. It is committed per Task instead, by memory_digest (). Operator-authored seed memory files MAY be listed as instruction_file entries.

config_digest is computed over the canonical CBOR encoding (or the JCS encoding, in the JSON form) of the entries array alone. It is the value that Execution Receipts reference. A Decision Point MUST block a call to a tool absent from the tool manifest committed by the configuration in force.

section.name: Unicode Normalization Before Digesting
section.t: Textual configuration inputs are a vector for instruction injection that is invisible to human reviewers. Before digesting any entry whose content is valid UTF-8, an Issuer MUST apply Unicode Normalization Form C , then process the following code points according to the normalization profile, then digest the resulting UTF-8 octets: U+200B, U+200C, U+200D (zero width space, non-joiner, joiner); U+2060 (word joiner); U+FEFF (including a leading byte order mark); U+E0000 to U+E007F (Tags); and the bidirectional controls U+202A to U+202E and U+2066 to U+2069.

Under profile 1 ("strip") the listed code points are removed. Under profile 2 ("reject") their presence is an error and no statement is issued until the content is corrected; profile 2 is RECOMMENDED for the system_prompt, instruction_file, skill and tool_description classes. Content that is not valid UTF-8 is digested over the raw octets. Normalization is for digesting only; whether the Harness also strips these code points from what it presents to the model is a Harness matter not asserted by this statement.

A Configuration Drift Statement SHOULD be issued whenever a new Configuration Integrity Statement replaces a previous one for the same agent. Drift is an ordinary event; its significance is for the Relying Party to decide.

section.name: Execution Receipt Statement
section.t: An Execution Receipt is the per-call record. One is produced at every Decision Point for every call, whatever the decision, including blocked calls; a refused call is recorded with the record_type of the action refused. Its Issuer, when registered individually, is the Evidence Service.

figure.sourcecode:
execution-receipt = { 1 => 5, ; aee-type 2 => uint, ; seq, per Evidence Chain, from 0 3 => bstr .size 32, ; prev_hash: record-hash of seq-1, ; or 32 zero octets when seq = 0 4 => record-type, ; record_type ? 5 => uint, ; parent_seq (see below) 6 => decision, ; decision 7 => digest, ; policy_pack_digest in force 8 => digest, ; config_integrity_digest in force 9 => tstr, ; agent_id: Runtime Identity in force 10 => principal, ; principal 11 => uint, ; task_seq: seq of the Task's task_start ? 12 => digest, ; request_digest ? 13 => digest, ; response_digest 14 => uint, ; ts, milliseconds since the Unix epoch ? 15 => bstr .cbor COSE_Sign1, ; agent_sig (per-call signature) ? 16 => tstr, ; target: model_id or tool name ? 17 => tstr, ; egress_host (lowercase A-label, no port) ? 18 => decision-point, ; decision_point ? 19 => uint, ; confirm_seq: the confirm it resolves ? 20 => tstr, ; caller_agent_id (admission only) ? 21 => caller-ref, ; caller_ref (admission only) ? 22 => admission-basis, ; admission_basis (admission only) ? 23 => [ + tstr ], ; actor_chain, least recent first ? 24 => bstr .size 32, ; principal_link ? 25 => tstr, ; txn: transaction identifier ? 26 => digest, ; memory_digest (task_start, task_end) ? 27 => subagent-ref, ; subagent ? 28 => uint, ; delegated_from (task_start only) ? 29 => digest ; call_digest } record-type = &( task_start: 1, task_end: 2, inference: 3, tool_call: 4, tool_result: 5, egress: 6, admission: 7 ) decision = &( allow: 1, block: 2, confirm: 3, record: 4 ) decision-point = &( model: 1, tool: 2, network: 3, ingress: 4 )
