section.t: The members have the following semantics.

dd.t: Define the Evidence Chain ().

task_start and task_end delimit a Task; inference records one model request/response pair; tool_call and tool_result record a tool invocation and its result; egress records a network connection made by a tool or by the Harness on the agent's behalf; admission records a Serving Party's decision on a call it received ().

For tool_call, the seq of the inference receipt whose response requested the call; for tool_result, that of the corresponding tool_call (for a confirmed call, its allow outcome); for egress, that of the tool_call (or inference) that caused it; for a task_start caused by an admitted call, that of the admission receipt. It MUST be less than seq and MUST reference a receipt of the required type. This is the causal link between what the model asked for and what the Harness did.

allow: the call proceeded. block: refused by policy. At the model door a block can follow forwarding when the decision depends on the response, for example when the responding model is not permitted or concurrent calls exceeded a limit; the response is then not passed to the agent. record: proceeded without policy evaluation. A call that the Harness observes only after another party executed it, such as a tool a model platform ran server-side, MUST be recorded as record, never allow or block, because no decision preceded it.

confirm: policy required confirmation from a Principal or operator before the call could proceed. It appears only on tool_call receipts. A confirm receipt MUST be followed by exactly one tool_call receipt with the same parent_seq, target, request_digest and Task that records the outcome: allow if confirmation was granted, or block if it was refused, not given before its deadline, could not be obtained, or was overridden by an operator halt. Until its outcome is recorded, the call is to be read as not having proceeded. An outcome MUST carry confirm_seq naming the confirm it resolves; a tool_call without confirm_seq is not an outcome. A tool_result for the call MUST NOT precede an allow outcome. A Task MUST NOT end while a confirm in it awaits its outcome; when a Task is closed, or the session is lost, with a confirm pending, the Evidence Service records the outcome as block first.
On an outcome, the seq of the confirm receipt it resolves. It MUST name an earlier confirm receipt with the same parent_seq, target, request_digest and Task, and MUST NOT appear on any other receipt.

The pack_digest and config_digest in force at the time of the call. Both MUST be present in every receipt, so that one receipt with its Bundle states the rules and configuration it was produced under.

The Runtime Identity under which the agent, or the Sub-agent named by subagent, is authenticating at the time of the call. It MUST be listed, with a validity window containing ts, in runtime_identities of the governing Agent Credential Statement or of the named Sub-agent's entry in it. On a Serving Party's chain it is the service_id or one of its runtime_identities. Receipts of one chain MAY carry different agent_id values as the agent moves between environments; the chain, not the identifier, is the unit of continuity. A Policy Pack MAY require agent_id to be constant within a Task.

Digests of the request and response octets as seen at the Decision Point: the model request and response for inference, the arguments and returned value for tool records. response_digest commits to the octets as received, before the Harness alters, truncates or withholds anything it passes to the agent. Digests require no parsing: a forwarded call whose response is an error, malformed or unparsable MUST still be recorded, with response_digest over the octets received, or absent if none were received. Content MUST NOT be included in a receipt ().
Time of production. Receipts in a chain MUST be non-decreasing in ts.

A COSE_Sign1 with detached payload, signed with the credential's agent_key, whose Sig_structure payload is the canonical encoding of the receipt map without key 15; its CWT Claims carry the agent identifier in iss and sub. It distinguishes a receipt the agent itself authorized from one the Harness recorded unilaterally, and MUST be verified when present.

The model_id or tool name, or for admission the operation requested; and, for egress, the host connected to. On a tool_call or egress receipt that carries call_digest, egress_host is REQUIRED and is instead the host named in the request: the host of the authority of the target URI, as the caller intended it. It is not the next network hop. Behind a forward proxy the host connected to is the proxy, every call would record the same host, and the service binding of would check nothing. Recording the host, not merely the decision, is what makes the exfiltration class in detectable after the fact.
See and .

The Actor Chain, Principal Link and transaction identifier of the call, on a tool_call or egress receipt for a call to another party and on an admission receipt (). txn has the meaning of the txn claim of . It answers the "transaction or request correlation identifier" required by Section 11 of .

On a tool_call or egress receipt for a call to another party, and on an admission receipt, a digest of the request as sent (by the caller) or as received (by the Serving Party), computed under the binding for the protocol in use. Unlike request_digest, which is over the octets as seen at the Decision Point and so differs between the two sides, both sides compute call_digest over the same representation. It is therefore equal for one call and different for calls that ask for different things. A receipt that carries it records exactly one request. A receipt for a protocol that has no binding carries no call_digest. A Serving Party computes its own value over the request it received and never takes it from the evidence presented ().

For HTTP, call_digest is SHA-256 over the deterministic CBOR encoding of the array [method, request-target, content-digest]. method is the request method as a text string. request-target is the path and query of the target URI in origin-form (), as sent, without normalization, as a text string; in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 it is the value of the :path pseudo-header field, which carries the same path and query. content-digest is the SHA-256 digest of the message content () as a byte string, or of the empty string if there is none; it equals the sha-256 value of a Content-Digest field () when one is present. Scheme and authority are excluded, because intermediaries rewrite them; the intended service is bound separately (). Other protocols define their own binding.

On task_start and task_end, a digest of the agent's memory state at that point, computed over a canonical serialization defined by the Harness and named in its published configuration. Changes between Tasks are thereby visible and attributable without blocking calls.

On every receipt produced for a Sub-agent, its subagent_ref and function, which MUST match an entry of the governing Agent Credential Statement, and optionally an instance number distinguishing concurrent instances. agent_sig on such a receipt is made with the Sub-agent's subagent_key where one is listed.
On a task_start, the seq of the task_start of the Task from which this Task was delegated within the same chain, for example to a Sub-agent ().

section.name: Evidence Chain
section.t: The record-hash of an Execution Receipt is SHA-256 over its canonical encoding (canonical CBOR, or JCS for the JSON form), including key 15 when present. An Evidence Chain is scoped to one Agent Credential or Serving Party Credential Statement and MUST begin with a receipt of seq 0 whose prev_hash is 32 zero octets. Each subsequent receipt carries in prev_hash the record-hash of the receipt with seq one less. seq MUST increase by exactly one. A receipt whose prev_hash does not match is not part of the chain.

task_seq names the Task: it is the seq of the task_start receipt that opened it, and a task_start carries its own seq. Every other receipt MUST name an earlier task_start with decision allow whose Task has not ended; a Task has at most one task_end, and no receipt names a Task after it. A receipt's parent MUST belong to the same Task, except that the parent of a task_start caused by an admitted call is that admission receipt; every receipt of a Task MUST carry the principal of its task_start. Receipts of different Tasks MAY interleave in one chain. An admission receipt belongs to no Task: its task_seq equals its own seq, and the Task rules do not apply to it.

A Task with delegated_from is a delegated Task. Its task_start MUST name an earlier task_start of a Task that has not ended, and MUST carry the same principal as that Task. Its policy_pack_digest MUST equal the parent Task's or name a registered pack whose parent chain () includes the parent Task's pack, so that the delegated Task's policy descends from the parent's; that a descendant is semantically stricter is asserted as described in . Whether its effective scope is no wider than the parent's cannot yet be checked mechanically ().

section.name: Admission
section.t: An Ingress Decision Point produces an admission receipt, with decision_point ingress, for every call it receives, whatever the decision. Its decision is allow or block; a refused call is recorded as block. The receipt records:

list.t: caller_agent_id: the Calling Agent's identity, where it was authenticated on the call;
principal: the Principal asserted by the Calling Agent, as the Serving Party validated it, hashed with the Serving Party's pepper if a natural person;
target and request_digest: the operation requested and the request as received;
call_digest: computed by the Serving Party over the request it received;
caller_ref, actor_chain, principal_link and txn, where received (); and

admission_basis: what the decision relied on. A Serving Party that enforces assurance MUST record it on every allow, with the Assurance Statement and level relied on, the registration, and when the status was checked and the value observed; it SHOULD also record a digest of the token presented.

section.t: A Serving Party MUST NOT admit an operation beyond what its policy permits for the principal of the transaction and for every Actor in actor_chain. A Serving Party evaluates every Actor in actor_chain against its own policy, as permits for informational claims. The Actor Chain is attribution, not authority: it records who is claimed to have acted, not that any hop held or narrowed authority. Evidence of what each hop did, and on what basis it was admitted, comes from the linked receipts on both sides of that hop and their admission_basis (), verified hop by hop; showing mechanically that authority narrowed at each hop needs a common representation of scopes (). Where authority itself must be carried across hops, delegation-chain mechanisms such as apply; this profile does not define one. The status of the Calling Agent's Assurance Statement and registration MUST be no older than the freshness the Serving Party's policy requires when the decision is taken. An agent whose Assurance Statement is RESTRICTED () is admitted only for operations within the restricted class.

A Serving Party that receives a cd value with a call () computes its own call_digest over the request it received, and MUST NOT use the presented value. It MUST refuse the call, recorded as block, when the two differ. A Serving Party MUST refuse a call whose caller_ref names a caller receipt that an earlier admission receipt in its own Evidence Chain already names, and records the refusal as block. The check and the recording of the admission MUST be atomic, so that concurrent requests carrying the same caller_ref cannot both be admitted. The check covers only the Serving Party's own Evidence Chain; what other Serving Parties have admitted is not visible to it, which is why also checks the service binding.

admission_basis.status_checked_at is the time of the status observation that the decision relied on. Where the token's cached status was used, it is the token's status_checked_at (). It is not the time of admission.

section.name: Linking Records Across Calls
section.t: A Calling Agent's tool_call or egress receipt for a call to another party carries txn, principal_link and actor_chain. The Actor Chain is the one the Calling Agent received with the request it is serving, or empty if it originated the request, with its own agent_id appended. The Serving Party's admission receipt for the call carries the same values and a caller_ref naming the Calling Agent's receipt.

txn, principal_link and actor_chain correlate the two records, but only call_digest and the service binding establish that they record the same call. A shared transaction, principal or session is not a match. A match is exact equality of digests over the same representation, computed by each side from the request it sent or received and never taken from the evidence presented, and a failed match is reported separately from verification and correlation failures. This follows the separation of correlation from matching in . The following rules apply:

list.t: caller_ref names a tool_call receipt with decision allow (for a confirmed call, its allow outcome) or an egress receipt, in either case one that carries call_digest, by the Issuer of the caller's Evidence Service, its seq and its record-hash. A connection-level egress receipt that does not record a single request cannot be named. At most one admission receipt names any one caller receipt.
The caller receipt's ts is not later than the admission receipt's ts plus a clock-skew allowance stated in the Serving Party's Policy Pack.

principal_link is SHA-256 over the octets of the token by which the Calling Agent presents the Principal's delegation on the call; for HTTP, the access token in the Authorization header field, not a Workload Identity Token or proof token. Both parties compute it from the same octets, so they are equal for the same call, while neither reveals the Principal. The caller's and the Serving Party's principal values differ when their peppers differ.
txn is equal on both sides and on every receipt the call causes, across the whole Call Chain.

actor_chain is equal on both sides, and its last entry equals both the admission's caller_agent_id and the caller receipt's agent_id. A Serving Party that is itself an agent appends its own agent_id on the calls it makes in the Task the admission caused.
call_digest is equal on both sides.

The caller receipt's egress_host is one of the hosts of the credential that scopes the Serving Party's chain: its Serving Party Credential Statement or, for a Serving Party that is an agent, its Agent Credential Statement. The comparison is between the host the caller named and the Serving Party's declaration, not between Host values as they arrive, so a gateway that rewrites Host does not break it.

section.t: A Calling Agent transmits these values with each call by means outside this document; defines them for HTTP. Records linked in this way form Linked Evidence Chains, verified as in .

section.name: Execution Epoch Statement
section.t: Registering every receipt as its own Signed Statement is permitted but is usually impractical. An Evidence Service MAY instead register an Execution Epoch Statement that commits to a contiguous segment of the chain.

figure.sourcecode: execution-epoch = { 1 => 6, ; aee-type 2 => tstr, ; agent_id 3 => uint, ; first_seq 4 => uint, ; last_seq 5 => bstr .size 32, ; first_prev_hash: prev_hash of first_seq 6 => bstr .size 32, ; last_hash: record-hash of last_seq 7 => bstr .size 32, ; epoch_root 8 => uint ; count = last_seq - first_seq + 1 }

section.t: epoch_root is the Merkle Tree Hash, as defined in with SHA-256, over the ordered record-hashes of receipts first_seq through last_seq. Because receipts are also hash-chained, first_prev_hash and last_hash allow adjacent epochs to be checked for continuity without their contents. A Relying Party in possession of a subset of an epoch's receipts verifies them with an inclusion path against epoch_root, using the inclusion proof algorithm of .

Epochs of one chain MUST NOT overlap and MUST be registered in order, and all carry in key 2 the agent_id of key 2 of the credential that scopes the chain, whatever Runtime Identity individual receipts carry, so that the continuity check of applies to the whole chain. An Evidence Service SHOULD close an epoch at every task_end and at a bounded interval, so that the time between a call and its appearance in the TS is bounded. That interval is an operational parameter that a Relying Party MAY require to be stated in a Policy Pack.

section.name: Assurance Statement
section.t: An Assurance Statement is a time-bounded assertion about an identified agent's declared purpose, effective capabilities, deployment and controls. It records the risk basis, assessment depth and, where required, operational monitoring. It is bound to the digests that determine behaviour.

figure.sourcecode:
assurance = { 1 => 7, ; aee-type 2 => tstr, ; assessor: Agent Assurance Assessor ID 3 => digest, ; agent_credential_digest: digest of the ; Agent Credential Statement payload 4 => digest, ; policy_pack_digest 5 => digest, ; config_integrity_digest 6 => tstr, ; suite_id (URI) 7 => tstr, ; suite_version 8 => &( pass: 1, fail: 2, partial: 3 ), ; result ? 9 => digest, ; report_digest of the full report 10 => validity, ; validity ? 11 => status-ref, ; status: Token Status List reference 12 => 1..4, ; assurance_level 13 => assessed-scope, ; assessed_scope 14 => risk-assessment, ; risk_assessment ? 15 => monitoring-summary, ; monitoring_summary 16 => tstr, ; logical_agent_id ? 17 => digest ; independence_declaration_digest } assessed-scope = { 1 => digest, ; capability_profile_digest 2 => digest, ; approved_model_scope_digest 3 => digest, ; approved_tool_scope_digest 4 => &( public-cloud: 1, private-cloud: 2, on-prem: 3, air-gapped: 4, edge: 5 ), ; deployment_class 5 => tstr, ; declared_purpose 6 => [ + tstr ], ; objectives 7 => [ + tstr ], ; intended_use 8 => digest, ; approved_data_scope_digest 9 => digest, ; approved_permission_scope_digest 10 => digest ; approved_delegation_scope_digest } risk-assessment = { 1 => tstr, ; scheme_id (URI) 2 => tstr, ; tier in that scheme 3 => bool, ; higher_risk 4 => digest ; risk_assessment_digest } monitoring-summary = { 1 => uint, ; period_start 2 => uint, ; period_end 3 => uint, ; review_frequency, seconds 4 => [ + monitoring-dimension ], ; coverage 5 => digest, ; evidence_digest 6 => uint, ; deviation_count 7 => &( continue: 1, reassess: 2, suspend: 3, withdraw: 4 ), ; disposition ? 8 => digest ; findings_digest } monitoring-dimension = &( purpose: 1, model: 2, tool: 3, data: 4, permission: 5, delegation: 6, policy: 7, configuration: 8, deployment: 9, control: 10, execution: 11 ) ; status-ref is the value of the "status" claim for CWT Referenced ; Tokens as defined in [I-D.ietf-oauth-status-list]. status-ref = { * any => any }
revocation = { 1 => 8, ; aee-type 2 => digest, ; subject_digest: digest of the ; payload of the revoked statement 3 => uint, ; reason_code (1 key-compromise, ; 2 superseded, 3 withdrawn, 4 other, ; 5 closed) 4 => uint, ; iat ? 5 => tstr ; reason }

section.t: The assessor value MUST equal the iss value in the protected CWT Claims of the Assurance Statement. The COSE signature therefore authenticates the identified Agent Assurance Assessor as the Issuer. The JSON member names for keys 12 through 17 are assurance_level, assessed_scope, risk_assessment, monitoring_summary, logical_agent_id and independence_declaration_digest. logical_agent_id MUST equal the referenced credential's logical_agent_id, and capability_profile_digest MUST equal that of the Agent Registration Statement the credential names, so that the agent is assessed against what was registered. The scope digests commit to the agent's effective models, tools, data, permissions and delegation powers. The approved model scope MUST identify each model by a dated version identifier, never by an alias that the provider can repoint, and by weights digest where the weights are available to the deployer. A change to either is a material change. capability_profile_digest commits to the complete capability profile, including the declared purpose, objectives and intended use repeated in keys 5 through 7. This profile defines the required coverage but not the document formats or a universal capability taxonomy.

scheme_id identifies a risk-classification scheme published by a Supervisory Authority (), and tier is meaningful only within that scheme. This profile does not define a universal risk scale. The scheme SHOULD consider autonomy, persistence (lifecycle_class), effective capabilities, access to sensitive data or resources, delegation powers, potential consequences and control effectiveness. The Agent Assurance Assessor applies the scheme; it does not define it. Any single trigger the scheme defines is sufficient to place an agent in the tier it names, and a tier can be raised but not lowered by the assessor. higher_risk records that, under the scheme, the independent-assessment and monitoring rules below apply; risk_assessment_digest commits to the rationale and inputs.

monitoring_summary is backward-looking. It states the completed monitoring period, coverage, maximum interval between reviews, evidence commitment, detected deviations and resulting disposition. The evidence MUST support monitoring for deviations from the assessed scope and approved controls, including policy violations and unexpected behaviour. A non-zero deviation_count requires findings_digest. The full findings MUST be investigated under the named suite; the summary intentionally avoids publishing sensitive operational details. A disposition other than continue means that the assessor no longer supports the assessment. Where a Supervisory Authority is designated for the scheme, the assessor reports suspend and withdraw dispositions to it, and the Supervisory Authority sets the status or withdraws the statement ().

section.name: Agent Identity Assurance Levels (AIAL)

texttable.title: Agent Identity Assurance Levels (AIAL)
texttable.c: The Responsible Entity declares that the agent meets the assessed scope.
Level 1 plus accepted RATS Evidence, such as an EAT , for the assessed runtime and Harness.
Level 2 plus a Third-Party Agent Assurance Assessor's review of the accepted RATS Evidence, capability profile, deployment and controls under the named suite.
Level 3 plus continuing operational monitoring, including registered Evidence Chains, for the stated period and coverage.

section.t: The assurance_level value is an Agent Identity Assurance Level (AIAL). These levels grade the assessment of an agent's purpose, capabilities, deployment and controls. They are not the Authenticator Assurance Levels of , do not express authentication strength, and SHOULD NOT be abbreviated as "AAL". "Identity" is in the name because the levels attach to an identified, registered Logical Agent (); they are closest in role to that guideline's Identity Assurance Levels, which grade proofing before a credential is issued. Following the same separation, this profile treats assessment depth, the strength of the binding between an agent and its credential key, and the security of identity propagation as independent dimensions. A level carries no statement about how the credential key is protected, nor about how the operator was verified; a Relying Party that requires a hardware-bound or attested key MUST require it separately in policy, for example through accepted RATS Evidence about key storage. A jurisdiction's profile MAY set key-custody and operator-verification requirements alongside a minimum level, as separate requirements.

At levels 3 and 4, the Agent Assurance Assessor MUST be a Third-Party Agent Assurance Assessor and MUST include independence_declaration_digest, committing to its signed declaration that it is independent of the Responsible Entity and the operator. Where the registered responsible_entity is an organization, assessor MUST also differ from it. A natural-person responsible_entity is a peppered digest that can never equal an assessor identifier, so no comparison is made in that case. Neither the declaration nor identifier inequality proves organizational independence; that remains a matter for the Supervisory Authority's accreditation of assessors. A Sub-agent has no level of its own: it operates under its parent's. Assessor recognition, suite suitability and accreditation remain Relying Party policy; the numbers have no meaning beyond this section.

At levels 3 and 4, accepted RATS Evidence and any resulting Attestation Results are the technical runtime evidence base for the independent assessment. The Third-Party Agent Assurance Assessor MAY perform the RATS Verifier role or consume Attestation Results from an accepted RATS Verifier. It MUST also evaluate the declared capability profile, deployment and controls; acceptance of RATS Evidence alone does not establish either level.

For higher_risk agents, a pass result MUST use level 4, include a monitoring_summary, use status checking, and have disposition continue. Before a required monitoring period is complete, the result MUST be partial, not pass. The Agent Assurance Assessor MUST issue a replacement statement at the required review frequency. A material change to purpose, capabilities, policy, configuration, deployment, controls or identity binding requires reassessment. A Relying Party MUST NOT accept operational assurance from a statement whose disposition is reassess, suspend or withdraw; the status and withdrawal that follow are set as described in and .

Higher-risk agents therefore require independent assessment and continuing operational monitoring. Assurance remains valid only while the applicable assessment, monitoring and reassessment requirements are satisfied. Each monitoring_summary covers a completed observation window, and replacement statements make monitoring continuing rather than a one-time probation period. Monitoring is an additional safeguard after the initial risk-based audit; it does not guarantee that an agent will never act maliciously. Its value depends on what the Harness and external evidence sources can observe and how reliably approved controls are enforced.

section.name: Supervision
section.t: The party that grants assurance does not monitor and act on its own grant: an assessor that suspended or restored its own statement would be judging its own decision. A Relying Party's policy, and where applicable a TS's Registration Policy, designates for each scheme_id the Issuer that acts as its Supervisory Authority. Where one is designated:

list.t: it publishes the scheme, including its risk triggers and the deviation classes that require immediate suspension;
the Token Status List referenced by an Assurance Statement under the scheme MUST be issued by it;
only it sets RESTRICTED or SUSPENDED, restores VALID, and withdraws an Assurance Statement under the scheme; and
the Agent Assurance Assessor issues verdicts and monitoring summaries and reports deviations to it.

section.t: A deviation detected during monitoring MUST be reported to the Supervisory Authority. For deviation classes the scheme marks as requiring it, the Supervisory Authority MUST suspend at once. For others it MAY first restrict the agent, and suspend once the deviation is confirmed, so that a single unverified finding does not take an agent offline. Where no Supervisory Authority is designated, the Agent Assurance Assessor performs these functions, and a Relying Party MAY refuse assurance under such a scheme.

RESTRICTED is Status Type 0x03, which reserves as application specific; this profile defines its meaning. A status list that can carry it MUST use bits of at least 2. While a statement is RESTRICTED, a Decision Point or Serving Party that enforces assurance MUST refuse operations above the risk class the scheme defines for restriction, and SHOULD let in-flight Tasks reach a safe end. While a statement is SUSPENDED, a Decision Point that enforces assurance MUST refuse further model and tool calls by the agent, a Serving Party that enforces assurance MUST refuse its calls, and a Relying Party MUST NOT accept the agent's operational assurance. Restriction and suspension are lifted only by restoring the status to VALID, or by a replacement statement.

A Supervisory Authority acting beyond its scheme, or whose key is compromised, can restrict or suspend any agent assessed under that scheme. Relying Parties accept a Supervisory Authority only for the schemes it is designated for.

section.name: Revocation
section.t: An Assurance Statement is revocable by either of two mechanisms, and a deployment MUST support at least one: a Token Status List referenced from key 11, in which status 0x01 (INVALID) withdraws the statement and 0x02 (SUSPENDED) or 0x03 (RESTRICTED) limits it (); or a Revocation Statement registered on the same TS whose subject_digest equals the digest of the Assurance Statement payload, issued by the Supervisory Authority designated for its scheme or by the Assurance Statement's Issuer. Where a Supervisory Authority is designated, the assessor's own Revocation Statements are limited to reason codes 1 (key-compromise) and 2 (superseded). A Revocation Statement MAY also revoke an Agent Registration, Model Provider, Agent Credential, Serving Party Credential or Policy Pack Statement, issued by that statement's Issuer.

Reason code 3 (withdrawn) records an adverse finding. Reason code 5 (closed) records an administrative retirement with no adverse finding, for example an agent retired by its Responsible Entity or a registration that expired without renewal. An agent is closed by a Revocation Statement with reason code 5 that revokes its Agent Registration Statement, issued by the Agent Registration Authority at the direction of the Responsible Entity or on expiry; the Issuer of each of its Agent Credential Statements likewise revokes them. Relying Parties MUST NOT treat closed as evidence of misconduct. withdrawn and closed are final: a closed or withdrawn agent can operate again only under a new registration and a new assessment. Restriction and suspension through the status list are the only reversible states.

section.name: Registration Policy
section.t: requires a TS to apply a Registration Policy and to make that policy transparent. A TS that accepts statements of this profile MUST perform the mandatory checks of and the following type-specific checks, keyed on the aee_type claim in the protected header. A failing check MUST result in refusal to register; with this is a 400 response with Concise Problem Details.

dd.t: The aee_type claim MUST match key 1 of the payload; the content type MUST be one of the statement media types of ; and the payload MUST be well-formed. sub MUST match the type-specific subject defined in .

validity.nbf MUST be less than validity.exp. The agent_key MUST be a COSE_Key whose alg is in the TS's accepted set. If the TS is configured to require it, credential_ref MUST be present. agent_id MUST appear in runtime_identities, and each entry's valid_from MUST be less than its valid_until. An Agent Registration Statement whose payload digest equals registration_digest MUST already be registered, and its logical_agent_id and responsible_entity MUST equal this credential's. If present, provider_statement_digest MUST be among that registration's provider_statement_digests. subagent_ref values MUST be unique, and each Sub-agent's runtime_identities entries MUST have valid_from less than valid_until.

If parent_pack_digest is present, a Policy Pack Statement whose pack_digest equals it MUST already be registered on this TS, and its layer MUST be strictly less than this pack's layer. The TS MUST NOT register a pack that references itself, directly or through its ancestors.
config_digest MUST equal the digest of the canonical encoding of entries. entries MUST be ordered by name in octet order and MUST NOT contain duplicate names. normalization MUST be 1 or 2.
Configuration Integrity Statements with config_digest equal to prev_config_digest and to new_config_digest MUST both already be registered for the same agent_id.

An Agent Credential or Serving Party Credential Statement for agent_id with the same Issuer, or an Issuer the TS's policy accepts for that agent, MUST already be registered. For an individually registered Execution Receipt, a Policy Pack Statement with pack_digest equal to policy_pack_digest MUST already be registered, and a Configuration Integrity Statement with config_digest equal to config_integrity_digest MUST already be registered, its registration preceding this registration. An Execution Epoch carries neither digest, so for receipts sealed in an epoch these two checks are made by the Relying Party (, steps 11 and 12). For an individually registered Execution Receipt, an admission receipt that carries caller_ref MUST carry call_digest, and a tool_call or egress receipt that carries call_digest MUST carry egress_host; for receipts sealed in an epoch, Linked Verification () makes these checks. For an Execution Epoch, count MUST equal last_seq - first_seq + 1, and if an epoch for the same agent_id and Issuer has already been registered, this epoch's first_seq MUST equal that epoch's last_seq + 1 and its first_prev_hash MUST equal that epoch's last_hash. The TS cannot check receipt contents it does not see; the precedence and continuity checks are what it can and MUST enforce.

assessor MUST equal the protected iss. Statements whose payload digests equal policy_pack_digest and config_integrity_digest MUST already be registered on this TS. The referenced Agent Credential Statement MUST already be registered, its logical_agent_id MUST match key 16 and sub, and capability_profile_digest MUST equal that of the Agent Registration Statement it names. At operational assurance level 3 or 4, independence_declaration_digest MUST be present and, where the registered responsible_entity is an organization, assessor MUST differ from it. validity.nbf MUST be less than validity.exp; scheme_id, tier, declared_purpose, objectives and intended_use MUST be nonempty. If present, a monitoring period MUST end after it starts and review_frequency MUST be non-zero. A higher-risk pass MUST meet the level 4, monitoring, status and disposition requirements of .

A statement whose payload digest equals subject_digest MUST already be registered. The Issuer of the Revocation Statement MUST be the Issuer of that statement or, for an Assurance Statement, the Supervisory Authority that the TS's policy designates for its scheme_id.

logical_agent_id MUST be a did:web identifier whose domain name equals the host of the protected iss (). lineage_id MUST be nonempty, and validity.nbf MUST be less than validity.exp. If prior_registration_digest is present, a registration with that payload digest and the same lineage_id MUST already be registered. If the TS's policy requires it, each of provider_statement_digests MUST name a registered Model Provider Statement.
validity.nbf MUST be less than validity.exp, and the service_key MUST be a COSE_Key whose alg is in the TS's accepted set.
model_id, provider and permitted_uses MUST be nonempty.

section.t: A TS MUST make these checks reproducible by Auditors as required by ; publishing the Registration Policy as a Signed Statement that cites this document by name and version is sufficient.

section.name: Bundle
section.t: A Bundle is the unit a Relying Party verifies. It is a CBOR map.

figure.sourcecode: aee-bundle = { 1 => [ + Transparent_Statement ], ; statements (RFC 9943 Sec. 7) 2 => [ * execution-receipt ], ; chain segment, ascending seq ? 3 => { * uint => inclusion-path }, ; seq => path into its epoch ? 4 => [ * bstr .cbor COSE_Sign1 ] ; Status List Tokens } inclusion-path = [ tree-size: uint, leaf-index: uint, path: [ * bstr .size 32 ] ]

section.t: Key 1 MUST contain, as Transparent Statements, the Agent Credential or Serving Party Credential Statement, the Agent Registration Statement an Agent Credential names, every Policy Pack Statement in the lineage of every policy_pack_digest in key 2, every Configuration Integrity Statement referenced, every Execution Epoch Statement covering a receipt in key 2 (or the receipt's own Transparent Statement), and any Assurance and Revocation Statements the producer wishes considered. Key 3 is REQUIRED for any receipt whose epoch is not wholly present in key 2. Key 4 carries a snapshot of each Status List Token referenced by an Assurance or Agent Registration Statement, or by a delegation_ref, for offline evaluation as of the snapshot time. Model Provider Statements MAY be included.
A Linked Bundle is an ordered array of Bundles, one for each Evidence Chain of a Call Chain, each sufficient on its own, with media type application/aee-linked-bundle+cbor. It is verified as in .

The media type of a Bundle is application/aee-bundle+cbor. A JSON form with the member names statements, receipts, proofs and status_tokens, Transparent Statements as base64url COSE_Sign1, has media type application/aee-bundle+json.

section.name: Verification
section.t: A Relying Party verifies a Bundle by the following steps. The steps are ordered; the first failure terminates verification with the named error. Verification requires the TS's public key(s), the trust anchors for Issuers the Relying Party accepts, and the Relying Party's own lists of accepted Agent Registration Authorities, Agent Assurance Assessors, levels and suites, and of the Supervisory Authority designated for each accepted scheme, all obtained out of band. No network access is required. A verifier that does not perform a step MUST NOT report PASS, and input that is malformed at any step fails that step rather than leaving the result undefined.

list.t: For every Transparent Statement in key 1, verify every Receipt in its receipts header (label 394) per against a trusted TS key, confirming that the Signed Statement is included in the VDS. On failure: E_RECEIPT_SIG.
For every Transparent Statement, verify the Issuer's COSE signature per against an Issuer key reached from a trust anchor. On failure: E_ISSUER_SIG.
For every Transparent Statement, check that the aee_type claim, the content type and key 1 of the payload agree and that the payload is well-formed. On failure: E_TYPE_MISMATCH.

Identify exactly one Agent Credential or Serving Party Credential Statement whose Issuer the Relying Party accepts and whose identifiers include the agent_id of the first receipt in key 2. Check that no Revocation Statement in the Bundle, from the same Issuer, names its payload digest. On failure: E_CREDENTIAL. For an Agent Credential, identify the Agent Registration Statement named by registration_digest, and check that its Issuer is an accepted Agent Registration Authority, that the domain of its logical_agent_id matches that Issuer (), that its logical_agent_id and responsible_entity equal the credential's, that its validity contains every receipt's ts, that any status it carries is 0x00 in the Status List Token in key 4 as of that token's snapshot, that no Revocation Statement from its Issuer names it, and that any provider_statement_digest in the credential is among its provider_statement_digests. On failure: E_REGISTRATION.

For each receipt in key 2, check that its agent_id appears, with valid_from <= ts < valid_until, in the runtime_identities of the credential or of the Sub-agent named by the receipt's subagent, or equals the service_id of a Serving Party Credential. On failure: E_RUNTIME_IDENTITY.

For each receipt in key 2, in ascending seq: check that seq is one greater than the preceding receipt's (or that the segment starts at a boundary stated by an Execution Epoch Statement), and that prev_hash equals the record-hash of the preceding receipt (or, for the first receipt, the first_prev_hash of its epoch, or 32 zero octets at seq 0). On failure: E_CHAIN_GAP or E_CHAIN_HASH.

For each receipt, locate the Execution Epoch Statement whose [first_seq, last_seq] contains its seq, or its individual Transparent Statement. If the whole epoch is present in key 2, recompute epoch_root and compare. Otherwise verify the inclusion path from key 3 against epoch_root. Check that consecutive epochs are continuous (first_prev_hash equals the previous last_hash). On failure: E_EPOCH_ROOT.

For each receipt with parent_seq: check that parent_seq < seq, that the referenced receipt is present in key 2, and that its record_type is the one required by . For each tool_result, check that a tool_call parent exists and is the parent of no other tool_result. On failure: E_PARENT_SEQ or E_PARENT_TYPE. Check the Task rules of for every receipt whose Task's task_start is in key 2. Check that every confirm_seq names an earlier confirm receipt in key 2 with the same parent_seq, target, request_digest and Task, and that each confirm has at most one outcome. A confirm without an outcome in key 2 fails only if its Task's task_end is in key 2, or a later receipt of that Task names the confirm receipt as its parent; otherwise the call is reported as not proceeded, which does not prevent PASS. On failure of the Task rules or of confirm/outcome pairing: E_TASK.
For each receipt, check that ts is within the validity of the credential identified in step 4 and is not less than the preceding receipt's ts. On failure: E_KEY_CURRENCY.

For each receipt carrying agent_sig, verify the COSE_Sign1 over the canonical encoding of the receipt without key 15, with the subagent_key of the Sub-agent named by subagent where one is listed, otherwise with the agent_key of the Agent Credential Statement or the service_key of the Serving Party Credential Statement. On failure: E_AGENT_SIG.

For each distinct policy_pack_digest in key 2, locate the Policy Pack Statement and walk parent_pack_digest to a root. Every pack on the path MUST be present as a Transparent Statement, layers MUST strictly increase from root to leaf, and the walk MUST terminate. On failure: E_POLICY_UNREGISTERED or E_POLICY_LINEAGE.

For each distinct config_integrity_digest in key 2, locate the Configuration Integrity Statement, recompute config_digest from entries, and check that the TS registration of that statement precedes, in the VDS, the registration of each receipt that references it, or of the Execution Epoch Statement that contains that receipt. Where the VDS exposes leaf indices through the inclusion proof, as RFC9162_SHA256 does, precedence is established by comparing them. On failure: E_CONFIG_UNREGISTERED or E_CONFIG_PRECEDENCE.

If the Relying Party requires assurance: for each (credential, pack, config) triple observed in key 2, locate an Assurance Statement whose assessor equals its protected iss, from an accepted Agent Assurance Assessor and suite, with result pass, sufficient operational assurance level, matching logical_agent_id and digests, and validity containing every receipt timestamp in that triple. Check the declared purpose and capability scope against policy. Check that its capability_profile_digest equals the registration's. At levels 3 and 4, require an accepted Third-Party Agent Assurance Assessor and independence_declaration_digest, and, where the registered responsible_entity is an organization, check that the assessor's identifier differs from it. Where a monitoring summary is present, require its disposition to be continue. For higher-risk agents, also require level 4 and a monitoring summary whose required coverage is accepted, and whose period_end is no more than review_frequency before each receipt time after conversion to seconds. On failure: E_ASSURANCE_BINDING, E_SCOPE_MISMATCH or E_MONITORING_STALE.

For each Assurance Statement relied upon: if it carries status, evaluate it against the Status List Token in key 4, verifying the token's signature and iat and, where a Supervisory Authority is designated for its scheme, that the token was issued by it. Require status 0x00; status 0x03 (RESTRICTED) is accepted only for receipts whose operations the Relying Party's policy places within the scheme's restricted class. In any case, require that no Revocation Statement from its Issuer or from the designated Supervisory Authority names its payload digest. On failure: E_ASSURANCE_STATUS or E_RESTRICTED.

For each receipt carrying subagent, check that subagent_ref and function match an entry of the governing Agent Credential Statement. For each delegated Task whose task_start is in key 2, check the rules for delegated Tasks in . On failure: E_SUBAGENT.

For each admission receipt, check that decision_point is ingress, that decision is allow or block, that every allow carries caller_agent_id, that the last entry of actor_chain, if present, equals caller_agent_id, and, if the Relying Party requires that the Serving Party enforce assurance, that every allow carries admission_basis with assurance_statement_digest, assurance_level and registration_digest. On failure: E_ADMISSION.
For each principal carrying a delegation_ref with status, evaluate it against the Status List Token in key 4 and require 0x00 as of that token's snapshot. On failure: E_DELEGATION_STATUS.
If all steps succeed, the result is PASS.

section.name: Linked Verification
section.t: A Relying Party verifies a Linked Bundle by first verifying each Bundle in it by steps 1 to 18, and then, for each admission receipt in one Bundle whose caller_ref names a receipt in another, checking that:

list.t: the named receipt is present, its record-hash equals caller_ref's, its seq matches, and its chain's Evidence Service is the Issuer named by caller_ref; on failure, E_CALLER_REF;
the named receipt and the admission both carry call_digest, and the values are equal; on failure, E_CALL_MISMATCH;

the named receipt's egress_host is present and is among the hosts of the credential governing the admission's chain: the Serving Party Credential Statement or, for a Serving Party that is an agent, the Agent Credential Statement. A credential without hosts fails this check; on failure, E_SERVING_HOST;

the named receipt is a tool_call with decision allow or an egress receipt, in either case one that carries call_digest, no other admission names it, and its ts is not later than the admission's ts plus the stated skew; on failure, E_CALLER_MISMATCH;
principal_link and txn are present and equal on both receipts; on failure, E_PRINCIPAL_LINK;
actor_chain is equal on both receipts, and its last entry equals the caller receipt's agent_id and the admission's caller_agent_id; on failure, E_ACTOR_CHAIN;

where the admission carries admission_basis naming an Assurance Statement or registration, that statement is the one the Calling Agent's Bundle relies on, at the level recorded; on failure, E_ADMISSION_BASIS; and

where the Serving Party is an agent whose Bundle is in the Linked Bundle, every call it makes in the Task the admission caused carries the same txn and an actor_chain equal to the admission's with its own agent_id appended; on failure, E_ACTOR_CHAIN.

section.t: Checks 2 and 3 follow check 1 so that a mismatch is reported as a mismatch and not as a missing receipt. E_CALL_MISMATCH and E_SERVING_HOST are reported separately from the verification errors of steps 1 to 18 and from the correlation errors of checks 4 to 8: they mean that the named receipt exists, but that the evidence does not show that the two records describe the same request sent to the same service.

A caller receipt for a call to another party that no admission in the Linked Bundle names, and an admission that names no receipt in it, are reported, not failed: the other party's records may simply be absent from the Linked Bundle.

section.name: Meaning of PASS
section.t: A PASS establishes that: the TS committed to each statement in its append-only VDS; each statement was signed by the named Issuer; the receipts form an unbroken chain sealed into that VDS; every call was recorded under a registered policy and configuration; each runtime identifier was declared for that time; and, where required, accepted identity and operational assurance claims matched the run. For higher-risk assurance, the accepted claim also cites a current completed monitoring period and has not been suspended or withdrawn. A PASS of Linked Verification establishes, in addition, that each linked pair of receipts commits to the same request, as represented by call_digest, sent to a host the Serving Party declared, for the same Principal, transaction and Actor Chain, by parties each of which verified on its own. It does not establish that the Serving Party is the service the caller meant where several services share that host, that every hop of the Call Chain is present, that an intermediary forwarded the request unchanged in the parts call_digest excludes, or that a Serving Party checked more than its admission_basis records.

A PASS does not establish that the Harness recorded every call, that a decision was correct, that an api-bound model was the one named, that a Policy Pack semantically tightens its parent, that monitoring observed every relevant behaviour, or that an Agent Assurance Assessor's suite is adequate. Harness completeness is the composition point with remote attestation. A Harness can produce RATS Evidence , for example an EAT whose measurements cover the image named by harness.digest; a Relying Party MAY require that Evidence, with the Agent Credential payload digest as nonce. This document does not define that binding.

section.name: Derivable Risk Facts
section.t: Two facts relevant to assurance can be tested from a verified chain without any further input, and a Relying Party or an Agent Assurance Assessor MAY compute them. The first is autonomy: over a window, the proportion of tool calls that proceeded without confirmation (an allow tool_call receipt that is not the outcome of a confirm) to those that required it. A chain in which every consequential tool call was confirmed by a Principal describes a different agent from one in which none was, even if both passed the same suite. The second is private inference: the model_binding mode of the governing credential as it applies to inference receipts. Mode weights-digest with no independent attestation of the runtime means the operator is the sole witness to which model ran; mode api-tee, or weights-digest accompanied by level 2 or higher attestation, provides a second witness. This document sets no thresholds for either fact; it notes that both are derivable so that Policy Packs and Agent Assurance Assessors can set them.

dd.t: Execution Receipts carry digests of requests and responses, never their content. Model prompts and tool arguments routinely contain personal data; the design keeps that data in the operator's custody and places only commitments on the TS.

A natural-person Principal, and a natural-person responsible_entity, is represented by SHA-256 over a pepper held by the statement's Issuer and the identifier. The pepper MUST be at least 16 octets of entropy, MUST NOT be registered on the TS, and SHOULD be rotated per deployment. The same Principal is linkable across receipts of one deployment by design, and not across deployments with different peppers.

principal_link lets the two parties to one call show that they recorded the same Principal without either revealing it, because it is a digest of a token both already hold. It does not link the Principal across calls unless the same token is presented again. txn and actor_chain correlate all hops of one transaction and reveal which operators' agents took part; parties SHOULD forward them only to the parties they call, and a Serving Party SHOULD register epoch roots rather than individual admission receipts. caller_ref reveals the caller's Evidence Service to the Serving Party.

call_digest is a digest of request content; where that content has low entropy, for example a payment amount sent to a known path, a party holding the receipt can confirm a guessed value by recomputing the digest. Registering epoch roots rather than individual receipts, as recommended under Retention, limits who holds the digest.

An Agent Registration Authority can link all agents of one Responsible Entity. Resolving a did:web identifier live tells the authority which agent is being checked and by whom; verifiers SHOULD rely on the registered statement in the Bundle instead. principal_assurance reveals how a Principal was verified, which can indicate residence or nationality; it SHOULD be carried only where a Serving Party's policy requires it.

target and egress_host are the only free-text members of a receipt and MUST NOT contain query, user, argument or parameter-value components; a tool name derived from an HTTP operation MAY carry its method and path template. Issuers MUST NOT place Principal identifiers or content in identifiers. Purpose, objective, intended-use and risk-tier strings SHOULD use concise categories or URIs rather than sensitive operational detail.
Statements registered on a TS cannot be removed. Operators SHOULD prefer registering epoch roots, which reveal only counts and digests, over individual receipts.
A Policy Pack at the jurisdiction or sector layer MUST NOT require that Execution Receipts identify natural persons in clear text.

A TS sees the protected header of every statement: Issuer, agent identifier, type and key identifier. Operators for whom the existence of an agent is sensitive SHOULD use opaque identifiers under their own trust domain.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The security considerations of and apply.

dd.t: A receipt is bound by prev_hash to its position and by agent_id and ts to its credential. Replaying it into another chain fails at step 6 of ; replaying it in the same chain fails because seq cannot repeat.

An operator who shows different chains to different Relying Parties is detected because both must be sealed into the same non-equivocating VDS (), and the continuity check in refuses the second epoch. This profile relies on the VDS properties and adds nothing to them.

A Harness that does not produce a receipt for a call leaves no trace. Mitigation is outside the chain: attestation of the Harness (), independent recording at the Serving Party by admission receipts (), and reconciliation of egress receipts against network telemetry. A call recorded by one party and not by the other is reported by Linked Verification when both chains are present; neither party can remove the other's record.

An agent serving several Principals can be induced to use one Principal's authority for another's request. Recording the Principal on every receipt of a Task, carrying the Actor Chain, and requiring a Serving Party to evaluate every Actor () make the substitution visible and let the Serving Party refuse it; they do not prevent an agent from misusing authority it legitimately holds.

A caller_ref, actor_chain or principal_link received with a call is the caller's claim until checked against the caller's registered chain. A caller_ref naming a receipt that does not exist fails E_CALLER_REF. One naming a different real call, for example a payment of another amount under the same token and transaction, fails E_CALL_MISMATCH, because the two call_digest values differ. One naming the same request sent to a service under a different host fails E_SERVING_HOST, because the caller's egress_host is not among the hosts the Serving Party declared. A reference replayed to the same Serving Party is refused at admission (); one replayed to a Serving Party under a different host fails E_SERVING_HOST. Either replay is also reported as E_CALLER_MISMATCH when both admissions are in the same Linked Bundle, because they name the same caller receipt. Actors removed from or inserted into the chain are detected when the chains of all hops are verified together.

A Serving Party that lists in hosts a host it does not control can be linked to calls meant for that host. The list is a signed claim by the Serving Party, and a Relying Party relies on it as it relies on the other claims of the credential. Front ends run by other operators are the subject of an open issue ().

One gateway host can front several services, and each lists that host in hosts, so E_SERVING_HOST cannot tell them apart. Where the gateway routes on the request path, call_digest binds that path, but the mapping from path to service is the gateway's own configuration, which a Relying Party trusts and which no receipt records. Two cases remain. A gateway that routes on something call_digest excludes, such as a header or tenant identifier, can deliver an identical request to either service. A request that reaches a service without passing through the gateway is admitted under the shared host. In both cases a caller reference meant for one service passes Linked Verification at the other, unless both admissions are in the same Linked Bundle and fail E_CALLER_MISMATCH. Operators of such gateways SHOULD route on the request-target, and services behind them SHOULD accept calls only through the gateway.

An admission decision based on a status observation older than the suspension of the agent admits a suspended agent. What matters is the age of the authenticated status observation, recorded as status_checked_at, and not the remaining lifetime of the token that carries it: a token with seconds left can carry an hour-old observation. A Serving Party bounds the age by the freshness its policy requires and SHOULD check the status list itself for operations its policy marks as high-risk.

Because a Serving Party records every call, including refusals, a caller can inflate its records. Serving Parties SHOULD rate-limit before the Ingress Decision Point; a call dropped there is not received and produces no receipt.

memory_digest makes changes to memory between Tasks visible after the fact; it does not prevent poisoned memory from influencing the next Task. A Policy Pack MAY require review of memory changes between Tasks for higher-risk agents.

A Decision Point that cannot evaluate a call MUST NOT let it proceed: for example an input over a size limit, a request it cannot parse, a response item it does not recognise, or an Evidence Service that cannot be reached. It MUST NOT evaluate a truncated or repaired form of the input instead. Where the Evidence Service is reachable, the refusal is recorded as block.

response_digest commits to what the Decision Point received, not to what the agent was given. A Harness that rebuilds, truncates or withholds a result before passing it on is not distinguishable from the receipt alone.

Compromise of the Evidence Service key allows forged receipts from the time of compromise; earlier epochs remain protected by the TS's Receipts. Compromise of the agent key allows forged agent_sig values but not forged receipts. Operators MUST register a Revocation Statement on compromise and SHOULD use short validity windows.

An attacker who obtains a workload identity in some trust domain cannot have receipts under it accepted for a Logical Agent unless the Agent Credential Statement lists that identity for that time (step 5 of ). Issuers SHOULD keep runtime_identities minimal and windows short.

The Evidence Service MUST authenticate each Decision Point that submits receipts. An agent session at a Decision Point bound only to a network address protects little, since addresses are shared and change. Sessions SHOULD instead be bound to possession of the agent key, for example with a per-request proof of possession or a certificate-bound session , so that a captured session identifier is useless without the key.

The principal in a receipt is asserted by the Evidence Service after it validated the Principal's token; the receipt does not carry a proof. An Evidence Service SHOULD retain, outside the receipt, a digest of each token as presented and of the key set it was verified with, so that an Auditor can repeat the validation. Token lifetime is judged at validation time, not at receipt time, since a Task can outlive the token that opened it; any clock-skew allowance MUST be bounded and stated in the Policy Pack or the Evidence Service's published configuration.

Loading a weaker Policy Pack produces receipts naming a different policy_pack_digest; a Relying Party that requires a specific root pack detects this at step 11. A Relying Party SHOULD reject chains whose policy_pack_digest changes within a Task.

The precedence check at step 12 ensures the Configuration Integrity Statement predates the receipts. The Harness MUST compute and compare digests at load time and SHOULD re-check them at a bounded interval during a run; a mismatch MUST produce a Configuration Drift Statement and a new Configuration Integrity Statement before any further receipt. Blocking calls to tools absent from the committed tool manifest () prevents a tool server from evading the commitment by not listing a tool.

Allowing egress to a list of trusted hosts does not stop exfiltration to an attacker-controlled account on an allowed host, or through path and query components. A receipt that records only decision: allow does not help an investigator. This profile therefore requires egress_host in egress receipts and request_digest over the full request, so that which host received data in which call is answerable from evidence rather than from the operator's account. It does not prevent the exfiltration.

The rule in makes invisible code points either irrelevant to the digest (profile 1) or a rejection (profile 2). It does not detect injection through visible but misleading text, homoglyphs, or content loaded at runtime outside the configuration set.

Level 1 can be self-asserted. At level 2, the Agent Assurance Assessor can still be the Responsible Entity, but accepted RATS Evidence adds technical runtime evidence. Levels 3 and 4 require a Third-Party Agent Assurance Assessor because an operator assessing controls it designed can share their assumptions and blind spots. The presence of an independence declaration is checkable, and identifier separation for an organization is only a weak signal; organizational independence, competence and accreditation are not established by this protocol.

Compromise of a Supervisory Authority's or Agent Registration Authority's key allows agents under it to be suspended, restricted or closed, or unregistered agents to appear registered. Relying Parties accept each authority only for the schemes or namespaces it is designated for, and the domain-match rule of prevents one authority from issuing identifiers in another's namespace.

A change of Responsible Entity produces a new registration and requires reassessment (). lineage_id lets an authority keep a history of adverse findings linked to the agent; it cannot prevent re-registration with another authority that does not share that history.

A Sub-agent without its own key signs as its parent, so its compromise is its parent's. A Sub-agent not listed in the credential fails verification; whether its declared function is within the Capability Profile is checked by the assessor, not by the verifier.

An assurance level and the protection of the credential key are independent. An agent assessed at level 4 whose key is held in software can be impersonated by any process that copies the key, and its records then carry that level. Relying Parties MUST NOT infer key protection from the level.

Monitoring detects only deviations visible in its declared coverage. An agent can behave maliciously within an approved scope, evade an instrumented Decision Point, or exploit a control that is present but ineffective. Relying Parties MUST evaluate coverage, evidence sources, review frequency and control enforcement rather than treating level 4 as a guarantee of safe behaviour.
This profile produces evidence about calls that pass through Decision Points. Behaviour entirely inside the model, inside a tool, or through a channel the Harness does not mediate is not recorded.

section.name: Related Work
section.t: This section states what each related document covers and how this profile composes with it. The intent is to coordinate, not to replace.

dd.t: Identity management functions and minimum audit fields for agents. This profile supplies the evidence format AIMS leaves open; maps the AIMS fields to the Execution Receipt and proposes a credential claim pointing at the Evidence Service.

RATS supplies roles and procedures for technical attestation, and EAT can convey claims about a measured runtime. This profile can bind that evidence to an identity or operational assurance claim, but does not replace RATS appraisal or turn runtime integrity into a behavioural guarantee.

SCITT provides statement transparency, WIMSE provides workload identity, and RATS provides technical attestation and the Verifier role. None defines a Third-Party Agent Assurance Assessor, a universal agent risk classification, a capability-audit method, or assessor qualification and accreditation criteria. This profile defines the assessor role and carries the identifiers, commitments and results needed for interoperability, while leaving recognition and accreditation to relying-party policy, applicable external governance, and possible future work coordinated across the relevant communities.

Roles and four record types (Interaction, Action, Delegation, Authorization Transition). The Execution Receipt is an Action Record at the Harness vantage, and the admission receipt is the corresponding record at the serving side; this profile is a candidate for that document's WI-3. A Delegation record composes with actor_chain and delegation_ref.

dl.dt: OAuth Token Exchange , Transaction Tokens and Identity and Authorization Chaining :

dd.t: Token Exchange expresses a chain of delegation by nested act claims; this profile records it as actor_chain; a Serving Party uses prior actors as policy input, as that specification permits, and takes evidence of what each hop did from per-hop receipts rather than from the act claim. Transaction Tokens propagate the principal of the transaction and a txn identifier along a Call Chain within one Trust Domain; this profile records txn on both sides of every call and extends the Call Chain across Trust Domains. Identity and Authorization Chaining carries identity across Trust Domains and leaves the format of transcribed claims open; the Actor Chain is one concrete record of what it carries. This profile complements these specifications with evidence and does not change them.

A JCS-canonicalized in-toto Statement in a DSSE envelope, richer per event and oriented to authorization decisions. defines an in-toto predicate type for Execution Receipts. An audit record can point to the Execution Receipt for the same call, or to the SCITT Receipt that registers it; the pointer associates the two records and dates neither of them ().

A JSON Capsule per action with disposition and an Effect Record, registered by Capsule ID. Its may/did distinction is finer than decision plus tool_result; a Capsule ID can be the request_digest of a tool_call receipt. This profile defers effect tracking to the Capsule.

JCS JSON receipts with Ed25519 signatures, a principal class, a lifecycle verdict and hash chaining. This profile shares that posture and adds credential, configuration and assurance statements and epochs. Alignment of verdict vocabularies is desirable.

The AgentInteractionRecord with inputs, outputs, reasoning traces and redaction receipts, and the same SCITT role mapping as here. This profile excludes content from statements; an AIR can be the retained content whose digest appears in a receipt.

dl.dt: Agent Passport System and Agent Audit Trail :

dd.t: A broad authority-and-evidence framework and a logging format respectively. This profile could serve as the evidence layer of the former and commits to entries of the latter by digest; no dependency is created.

Composes heterogeneous evidence for one consequential action, and separates native verification, acceptance and material-action matching. This profile adopts its separation of correlation from matching for linked receipts (). An admission or caller receipt that carries call_digest can be a native artifact that an EP-AEC evaluation composes. The reference is informative; this document does not depend on EP-AEC.

User-signed credentials expressing purchase authorization. A Mandate is an input to a tool_call; its digest belongs in request_digest, and the confirmation it embodies corresponds to decision confirm.

section.name: Open Issues
section.t: This section is to be removed before publication as an RFC.

list.t: Delegation scope: a mechanical test that a delegated Task's, or a later Actor's, effective scope is no wider than its parent's needs a common representation of scopes (, ).
Supervisory Decision statement: a statement by which a Supervisory Authority grants, restricts, suspends, restores or withdraws assurance.
Trust List statement: a statement by which a Supervisory Authority registers the assessors, schemes and foreign authorities it accepts.
Registering RESTRICTED in the OAuth Status Types registry instead of using the application-specific value 0x03.
A registry of record types, so that other profiles can extend them.
A reputation statement linked through lineage_id, and whether identifier forms other than did:web should be allowed for logical_agent_id.
Whether Serving Parties should also be registered by an authority.

Representation mapping: a defined mapping between different representations of one request, including proxies that rewrite the path, or a statement issued by a proxy that records what it forwarded (). call_digest compares the request as sent with the request as received and cannot match a request that an intermediary changed.

Front ends run by other operators, and shared front ends: whether hosts in the Serving Party's own credential is enough, or whether a proxy run by another operator should sign its own forwarding statement. A host also does not identify one service where a gateway fronts several (). Candidate designs are a path prefix on each hosts entry, which a Serving Party can enforce but a verifier cannot check because receipts do not carry the path, and a forwarding statement signed by the gateway naming the backend it routed the call to. A third is a handoff from the gateway to the effect boundary, as in : only the gateway that accepts the call signs, under a key the Relying Party pins, binding the action digest and the executor, so other intermediaries need not sign. This is the question put to the SCITT list.

section.name: Implementation Status
section.t: This section records the status of known implementations per and is to be removed before publication as an RFC.

Sijil's record model is the basis of the Execution Receipt; no export to the encoding defined here exists yet. Implemented: Harness-side Decision Points (model and tool doors); a hash-chained, signed record of every call, with Tasks, refusals and separately recorded approvals; and an offline verifier that checks the chain, the Task rules, and declared runtime identities with agent registration, key rotation proofs and revocation. Not implemented: COSE wrapping, epochs, Bundles, registration through , per-call agent_sig, validity-window identity checks, Assurance Statement checks, Principal peppering, and everything this revision adds: Agent Registration, Model Provider and Serving Party Credential Statements, Sub-agent records, memory_digest, Supervisory Authority status, admission receipts, linking across calls and Linked Verification, with call_digest, hosts and the matching and service-binding checks that this revision adds to it. A separate script generates the vectors in . Maturity: prototype. Licence: verifier, agent guard and rule packs Apache 2.0; other components Business Source License 1.1. The pack and configuration digests are over the octets {"pack":"example-serving-pack","v":"1.0.0"} and over one tool_manifest entry for openapi.json. The principal is hashed with the Serving Party's pepper serving-pepper-0001, so it differs from the caller's, while principal_link and txn are equal on both sides. The admission carries the same call_digest as receipt seq 3, which the Serving Party computed over the request it received, and seq 3's egress_host is among the Serving Party's hosts. section.name: Changes since -00
section.t: This section is to be removed before publication as an RFC.

list.t: Added call_digest (Execution Receipt key 29) and its HTTP binding, which covers the method, the path and query, and a digest of the content, and excludes scheme and authority ().
Added hosts to the Serving Party Credential (key 7) and the Agent Credential (key 15), required where the chain contains an admission receipt that carries call_digest (, ).
egress_host is required on a tool_call or egress receipt that carries call_digest, and on such a receipt records the host named in the request, not the next network hop ().
caller_ref may name only a receipt that carries call_digest ().
A Serving Party computes its own call_digest, and refuses a call whose cd differs. A Serving Party MUST refuse a caller reference it has already admitted ().

Linked Verification checks that call_digest is equal on both sides and that the caller's egress_host is among the Serving Party's hosts, reported as E_CALL_MISMATCH and E_SERVING_HOST (). The checks are renumbered.
Reworded the meaning of a PASS of Linked Verification () and corrected the claim in that every forged caller reference fails verification.
admission_basis.status_checked_at is the time of the status observation relied on, not the time of admission (); status freshness is judged by the age of that observation ().
Registration Policy requires call_digest on an admission receipt that carries caller_ref, and egress_host on a tool_call or egress receipt that carries call_digest ().
Added a privacy note on guessing low-entropy content from call_digest ().
Stated that hosts shows the caller named a declared host, not which service it meant where one gateway host fronts several services, and added the remaining cases to and Open Issues.
Added EP-AEC to Related Work, Open Issues for representation mapping and for front ends run by other operators, and Iman Schrock to the Acknowledgements.

Added a Shared front ends entry to : a gateway host shared by several services does not identify one of them, and call_digest binds the path while the mapping from path to service is trusted configuration that no receipt records. The front-ends open issue lists path prefixes, a gateway-signed forwarding statement and a handoff signed by the accepting gateway as candidate designs.

An audit record's pointer to an Execution Receipt or its SCITT Receipt dates neither record, and is no longer described as correlation.externalAnchor (). Updated the audit-record reference to -02 and added Sankalp Gilda to the Acknowledgements.

Moved the WIMSE architecture to the informative references: the profile builds on it, and the terms it borrows are used as described there. Updated the references to draft-ietf-wimse-identifier-04 and draft-sharif-agent-audit-trail-09.

A Serving Party evaluates every Actor against its own policy, as RFC 8693 permits for informational claims; the claim that this goes beyond RFC 8693 is removed. The Actor Chain is stated to carry attribution, not authority, with evidence of each hop taken from per-hop receipts and delegation-chain mechanisms referenced for carrying authority. The Introduction notes that showing that no intermediary used broader authority also needs a common representation of scopes.
Regenerated the test vectors: receipt seq 3, the admission receipt and the Serving Party Credential changed, and so did every value derived from them ().
